title: A flag is not a verdict.
subtitle: Count the flagged group before deciding how much a positive signal means.
subject: Mathematics · conditional probability
limits: This is a hypothetical factory with exactly specified frequencies, not measured performance or a medical test. Population strip uses the whole batch. Detail bars name their local denominators; collection bars use one common count scale, then expand to all flags. Detector rates are conditional on item status.
hook: A factory flags items for inspection. A good detector can still flag many sound items when defects are rare.

sources.title: OpenStax · Conditional probability
sources.locator: Conditional probability uses the conditioning event as its denominator.

steps.title: Start with the batch
steps.say: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. The hypothetical batch has 100 defective items and 9,900 sound items. Each rate starts with its own population.
steps.sayText: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. The hypothetical batch has 100 defective items and 9,900 sound items. Each rate starts with its own population.
steps.note: Hypothetical exact frequencies; every denominator names its group.

steps.title: Select within defective items
steps.say: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. The detector flags 90 of the 100 defective items. Its 90% hit rate leaves 10 defective items missed.
steps.sayText: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. The detector flags 90 of the 100 defective items. Its 90% hit rate leaves 10 defective items missed.

steps.figureLabel: Batch: 100 defective and 9900 sound. 90 true flags and 10 missed defective.

steps.title: Select within sound items
steps.say: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. Five percent of 9,900 sound items gives 495 false flags. A smaller rate can produce more flags because its population is larger.

steps.title: Collect only flags
steps.say: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. Move the 90 true flags and 495 false flags into one group. Leave 9,415 unflagged items outside, including 10 missed defects.

steps.figureLabel: Batch: 100 defective and 9900 sound. 90 true flags and 10 missed defective. 495 false flags. Selected: 585 flags; excluded: 9415.

steps.title: Change the denominator
steps.say: Worked example: base 1%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. Expand the same selected group. Its count stays 585. The defective share is 90 divided by 585, or 15.4%.

ask.q: Which denominator answers defective among flagged items?
ask.why: A flag selects all 585 flagged items, including false flags.

steps.figureLabel: Batch: 100 defective and 9900 sound. 90 true flags and 10 missed defective. 495 false flags. Selected: 585 flags; excluded: 9415. Defective among flags: 90/585, 15.4 percent.

steps.title: Change the base rate
steps.say: Worked example: base 10%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. At a 10% defect rate, the same detector gives 900 true flags and 450 false flags. Of 1,350 flags, 66.7% are defective.
steps.sayText: Worked example: base 10%, hit 90%, false flags 5%. At a 10% defect rate, the same detector gives 900 true flags and 450 false flags. Of 1,350 flags, 66.7% are defective.

steps.figureLabel: Batch: 1000 defective and 9000 sound. 900 true flags and 100 missed defective. 450 false flags. Selected: 1350 flags; excluded: 8650. Defective among flags: 900/1350, 66.7 percent.

steps.title: Remove false flags
steps.say: Worked example: base 10%, hit 90%, false flags 0%. With zero false flags, all 900 flags are true. Yet 100 defective items remain missed. Precision is 100%; hit rate is still 90%.

scenes.say: The hypothetical batch has 100 defective items and 9,900 sound items. Each rate starts with its own population.
The detector flags 90 of the 100 defective items. Its 90% hit rate leaves 10 defective items missed.
Five percent of 9,900 sound items gives 495 false flags. A smaller rate can produce more flags because its population is larger.
Move the 90 true flags and 495 false flags into one group. Leave 9,415 unflagged items outside, including 10 missed defects.
Expand the same selected group. Its count stays 585. The defective share is 90 divided by 585, or 15.4%.
At a 10% defect rate, the same detector gives 900 true flags and 450 false flags. Of 1,350 flags, 66.7% are defective.
With zero false flags, all 900 flags are true. Yet 100 defective items remain missed. Precision is 100%; hit rate is still 90%.
